headline: President Trump returns to the campaign trail with just 12 days until the midterms.
A 74-year-old retired American teacher, Steven Hubbard, has been freed from a Russian prison and returned to U.S. soil after more than four years detained.
Russia described Hubbard's release as a gesture of goodwill, and President Trump said the Russians did not ask for anything in return while noting he waived new sanctions against Russia.
U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff is facing criticism, including from Republican Senator Thom Tillis, for thanking Vladimir Putin for freeing Hubbard, while Vice President JD Vance defended Witkoff.
President Trump is facing bipartisan blowback over a diesel fuel deal with Russia aimed at addressing high prices ahead of the midterms, an issue that came up in last night's Kansas Senate debate.
President Trump reacted to Wall Street Journal reporting that Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Ukraine's Starlink system that hampered Ukrainian drone operations, saying he was not involved.

Fallout is growing over a controversial multimillion-dollar Ohio governor's race ad from Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy featuring his opponent Amy Acton's estranged mother, with Vice President JD Vance defending the ad.
Neil Bush, brother of former President George W. Bush, said he voted for Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico in Texas, citing deep concern about Ken Paxton's record.

Hundreds of thousands of taxpayer dollars, including $350,000 in contracts for mobile live cameras, are being spent to protect construction projects around Washington, D.C., that were President Trump's ideas.
Alaska's Senate race between Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Tola could hinge on the cost of living, with gas prices soaring above $8 a gallon in remote communities like Bethel.

An AI program detected a potentially dangerous vulnerability in PHP computer code used by nearly 70% of the internet, forcing some major websites and European government sites offline until a fix was in place.
The Vatican says 71-year-old Pope Leo will not need further treatment after tests showed his lung cancer was low, following surgery to remove part of his lung last week.
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty after a jury found the company misled consumers about data privacy in a case involving Cambridge Analytica, and Meta vows to appeal.

The parents of a 13-year-old boy killed while riding an electric motorcycle in Garden Grove, California, are facing child endangerment charges, with the Orange County D.A. saying they ignored warnings about his dangerous riding.
About 7 million people in the Southwest are under a flood watch, with severe weather including damaging wind, hail and possible tornadoes expected in Phoenix and Tucson.
A woman from Alabama is charged with threatening to kill President Trump before he was set to attend the Georgia-Alabama football game in Tuscaloosa.
Severe storms and flooding hit multiple states, prompting water rescues in Los Angeles County and a second tornado watch in parts of Arizona.
Retired NYPD detective Victor Romero was granted $1 million bail after being charged with manslaughter in the road-rage shooting death of Kuran Irvine on the George Washington Bridge.

Backlash grows over a Republican ad featuring the estranged mother of Ohio Democratic governor candidate Amy Actton, with Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine urging the ad be taken down while President Trump defends it.
Teacher Becky Drury describes playing dead after being shot at close range during the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon.
A Lauderdale, Florida police officer, Brian Siguros, is charged with stealing the identity of a dead man, Dennis West, and living in his home for years.
Looksmaxxing influencer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, pleaded not guilty to rape and other charges in Massachusetts.
Retired American school teacher Steven Hubbard returned to Texas after being freed by Russia, hours before Russia launched a deadly missile and drone attack on Kyiv.
A small plane made an emergency landing on Interstate 80 outside Reno, Nevada, forcing the closure of westbound lanes; the pilot was unhurt.
The mayor of Pennsauken, New Jersey, charged at a critic during a town hall meeting and was eventually escorted out.
Actress Dame Judi Dench says her worsening eye condition has forced her to stop working.
The hockey world mourns former NHL All-Star Ron Duguay, who died at 69 after battling stage 4 colon cancer.
The New York City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending an industry operating in the city since 1858.
Actor Tom Skerritt, known for roles in MASH, Alien, Top Gun, Steel Magnolias and Picket Fences, died of natural causes at 93.
